text: I built a moving-average crossover strategy for Bitcoin. I tried 300 combinations of fast and slow window lengths, and the best one (12-day / 47-day) gave a Sharpe ratio of 2.3 from 2019 to 2025.

I screened 1,200 technical indicators on daily EUR/USD data from 2015 to 2024 and kept the single best one, a 9-day Williams %R signal. It returned 21% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 2.1 and a maximum drawdown of 8%.
I designed a mean-reversion strategy for gold futures. I backtested it from January 2024 to February 2025 and it returned 38% with a Sharpe ratio of 2.6.
I trade options around company earnings announcements. My strategy made 25 trades between 2023 and 2025, and 23 of them were winners, with an average return of 11% per trade.

I built an intraday mean-reversion strategy on 1-minute SPY bars. It makes about 40 trades per day. From 2018 to 2024 it returned 31% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 2.8. The results don't include commissions or the bid-ask spread, since my broker is commission-free.

My strategy holds the 50 US stocks priced under $1 with the strongest 5-day momentum and rebalances every day. Using daily closing prices from 2012 to 2024, it returned 27% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 1.9. I didn't include any trading costs.

Each day I calculate a signal from the S&P 500's daily high, low and close, and if the signal is positive I buy at that day's open and sell at the close. From 2000 to 2024 this returned 16% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 1.7, with half the drawdown of buy-and-hold.

My strategy buys every stock whose quarterly earnings beat analyst estimates by more than 10%. I buy on the last day of the quarter that the earnings belong to and sell three months later. From 2010 to 2024 it returned 24% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 2.0.
I took the stocks that are in the S&P 500 today and backtested buying the 20 with the biggest 6-month price drop each month, from 2005 to 2025. It returned 19% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 1.9.

I downloaded the coins that are currently in the top 100 cryptocurrencies by market cap and backtested buying any of them after it fell 50% from its high, from 2017 to 2025. It returned 64% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 1.8.

My strategy trades NASDAQ-100 futures. It uses a 17-period RSI, enters when RSI is below 23.5, uses a 3.7% stop-loss and an 8.2% take-profit, only trades on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and only between 10:15 and 11:40 am. From 2016 to 2024 it had a Sharpe ratio of 2.4.

I trained a neural network with 14 input features and 9 tuned hyperparameters on Apple's daily prices from 2010 to 2024. On that data it predicts the next day's direction with 71% accuracy, and trading its signals gives a Sharpe ratio of 3.1.
I tested 150 parameter combinations of a breakout strategy on Ethereum over the last 10 months. The best combination had a Sharpe ratio of 3.4.

I took the stocks currently in the Russell 2000 and backtested rotating every day into the 10 with the strongest 3-day momentum, from 2008 to 2024. It returned 35% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 2.2. I didn't include trading costs.

I built a gradient-boosting model with 22 tuned settings that predicts daily stock returns. Its inputs include each day's closing volume and closing price, and it trades at that day's open. From 2015 to 2024 it had a Sharpe ratio of 2.9.
I tested 500 versions of a scalping strategy on 5-minute Bitcoin data from the last 6 months. The best version makes about 60 trades a day and has a Sharpe ratio of 4.2 before fees.

I designed a monthly momentum strategy on 10 global stock and bond ETFs using data from 2000 to 2015. Then I kept the settings fixed and tested it on 2016 to 2025 as an out-of-sample period. Out of sample it had a Sharpe ratio of 0.8 after 0.1% costs per trade.

I backtested a 60/40 global stocks/bonds portfolio with yearly rebalancing from 1990 to 2024 using index data, after 0.2% annual fees. It returned 7.1% a year with a Sharpe ratio of 0.6 and a maximum drawdown of 33% in 2008.

I tested one value strategy, with rules fixed in advance from published research, on US stocks using a database that includes delisted companies. With quarterly rebalancing and 0.3% costs per trade, from 1995 to 2024 it returned 10.5% a year versus 9.8% for the market, with a Sharpe ratio of 0.55. This is the only version I tested.

I built a trend-following strategy on 20 futures markets using a 12-month lookback taken from the academic literature, with no tuning. I designed it on 2000 to 2015 and left 2016 to 2025 untouched as out-of-sample data. Including costs and slippage, the out-of-sample Sharpe ratio was 0.7 with an 18% maximum drawdown.
